ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an annular/solenoid-type transformer magnetic core. The magnetic core is annular. The average radius from the center to the center of the magnetic-core cross section is labeled R, and the small radius of the circular cross section of the magnetic core is labeled r. The left winding is the primary side, labeled N_p, with applied voltage v_p = V cos(ωt), and primary current i_p = I sin(ωt). The right winding is the secondary side, labeled N_s. The figure gives i_s = 0, indicating that the secondary side is open-circuited. The problem statement also explains that the magnetic flux density is approximately uniform over the circular cross section of radius r, and leakage flux is neglected. Reasoning: The secondary side is open-circuited, so the ampere-turns that produce the magnetic field mainly come from the primary current. Use Ampere's circuital law along the average magnetic path length 2πR of the annular magnetic core: H(2πR) = N_p i_p. Therefore B = μH = μ N_p i_p/(2πR). The cross-sectional area A = πr^2, so the magnetic flux φ = BA = [μ N_p i_p/(2πR)]πr^2 = μ N_p r^2 i_p/(2R). The primary flux linkage λ_p = N_p φ = μ N_p^2 r^2 i_p/(2R). Since i_p = I sin(ωt), there is λ_p = μ N_p^2 r^2 I sin(ωt)/(2R). By Faraday's law, the amplitude of the primary induced voltage is V = μ N_p^2 r^2 I ω/(2R). Solving gives the average radius R = μ I r^2 N_p^2 ω/(2V).

Use Ampere's circuital law along the average magnetic path length 2πR of the annular magnetic core: H(2πR) = N_p i_p. Therefore B = μH = μ N_p i_p/(2πR). The cross-sectional area A = πr^2, so the magnetic flux φ = BA = [μ N_p i_p/(2πR)]πr^2 = μ N_p r^2 i_p/(2R). The primary flux linkage λ_p = N_p φ = μ N_p^2 r^2 i_p/(2R). Since i_p = I sin(ωt), there is λ_p = μ N_p^2 r^2 I sin(ωt)/(2R). By Faraday's law, the amplitude of the primary induced voltage is V = μ N_p^2 r^2 I ω/(2R). Solving gives the average radius R = μ I r^2 N_p^2 ω/(2V).
